subject: Poisoned-name veto fallback: section-let-bound name needed as the veto global is never defvar'd → unbound at load (FIX MEASURED s384, blocked on #299)
description:
Found s329 (probe, crashes LOUDLY in every era). Shape: file-level embedded `open my $fh, ...` + a named sub that (a) freely references $fh via a HIDDEN use (`<$fh>` readline / "$fh" interp — invisible to Symbol-token scans) and (b) also let-binds the same name somewhere. The veto fires correctly, but _forward_global_decls refuses to declare a section-let-bound name, so the fallback global never exists: "$fh is unbound".

FIX IS MEASURED (s384, then reverted with #291): drop that exclusion in FILE mode — `_forward_global_decls`'s `$lb` becomes `$free_out ? ($seg_lex // {}) : {}`. Since the flip a `p-defcell` is a symbol macro that a `let` of the same name shadows, so declaration and lexical coexist; the exclusion's only cause (a `defvar` proclaims the symbol special and poisons the section's own `let`s) died with the flip. EVAL mode keeps the exclusion — there the list is the p-eval-thunk's capture PARAMETERS from the caller, not declarations.

VERIFIED with that one-line change: both s329 probes run identical to perl, and both crash "unbound" without it. Sweep TOTAL went 18498 -> 18529 (+31).

BLOCKED ON #299: the same change costs 5 closure.t rows for reasons not yet identified. Land #299's diagnosis, then this closes with the enabler.

Probes (perl prints got:<hostname> / i1i2 a:<hostname>):
  probe A: open my $fh, '<', '/etc/hostname' or die; sub tricky { my $line = <$fh>; { my $fh = "shadow"; } chomp $line; return "got:$line" } print tricky(), "\n";
  probe B: open my $fh, '<', '/etc/hostname' or die; sub looper { my $s = ""; for my $fh (1..2) { $s .= "i$fh" } return $s } sub after { for my $fh (1..2) { } my $l = <$fh>; chomp $l; return "a:$l" } print looper(), " ", after(), "\n";
A self-contained version of probe A is already a guard row in Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t (it currently passes via the rename, and must keep passing after the enabler).
